name: Tuscan

ancestors.notes: Standard Italian is based on Tuscan; the dialect and standard share the same parent.

notes: Tuscan. The dialect of Tuscany that is the historical basis of standard Italian. Distinguished from the standard primarily by GORGIA TOSCANA: intervocalic voiceless stops → fricatives (/p/→[ɸ], /t/→[θ], /k/→[h]). Also features stronger raddoppiamento sintattico. The open/close mid-vowel distinctions are most consistently maintained here (Giannelli 2000, Rohlfs 1966). GRAPHEMES: the grapheme table and its positional readings come from it-IT through graphemes_base, because the variety writes standard Italian spelling. ⟨c g⟩ read [tʃ dʒ] before ⟨e i⟩ and [k ɡ] elsewhere: cielo [ˈtʃɛːlo], gelo [ˈdʒɛːlo] (Bertinetto & Loporcaro 2005, JIPA 35(2), p. 133). ⟨i u⟩ before a vowel are the glides [j w]: pieno [ˈpjɛːno], chiave [ˈkjaːve], guida [ˈɡwiːda] (p. 139, Table 2 on p. 138). The spec keeps its own ⟨s⟩ and ⟨z⟩ readings and does not take the it-IT positional ones. The it-IT intervocalic [z] is the Standard Northern value. For Florence the source records the lexical [s]/[z] contrast of chiese, which the Northern pronunciation levels out (p. 133). The it-IT word-initial [dz] for ⟨z⟩ has no Tuscan source here, so ⟨z⟩ keeps [ts] first. The allophone map keeps the Florentine deaffrication of intervocalic /tʃ/ as a variant: pace [ˈpaːʃe] (p. 135).

sources.author: Bertinetto, P.M. & Loporcaro, M.
sources.title: The sound pattern of Standard Italian, as compared with the varieties spoken in Florence, Milan and Rome
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association
sources.notes: JIPA 35(2). Illustration of Standard Italian; states the preconsonantal /s/ voicing agreement and documents the Tuscan/Northern split in intervocalic ⟨s⟩. Table 2 (p. 138) and p. 139 give the opening and closing diphthongs and the hiatus that the stress diphthongs list follows; p. 137 gives the two equal vowels in hiatus.
